current_bottleneck: 289b showed that a learned latent state fixes much of the direct observation-space collapse from 289a, but autoregressive rollout still collapses variance: the one-step latent predictor is usable while generated-state rollout becomes too smooth, too low-variance, and too weak on cointegration and jumps.
last_result_summary: Iteration 120 ran 289b-v0 and got 2/11, passing surface and block_ar. It materially improved corr_ratio, rank_ratio, MR ratio, and cell MAE versus 289a, but change KS fell to 0/25 and pathwise jump scale collapsed further. A teacher-vs-rollout probe showed the core problem is rollout variance collapse, not a dead one-step model.
next_step_recommendation: Implement 289c-v0: keep the deterministic latent world-model Stage A family, but replace the shallow state update with an explicit observation encoder feeding the recurrent latent transition at every generated step.
current_best_model: 277d-v0, 279a-v0, 281a-v0, 281b-v0, and 282b-v0 are the current overall co-frontiers at 5/11 in the two-level reset.
current_best_note: 282b is still the cleanest current Stage B objective frontier at 5/11, but 284b and 285a strengthen the conclusion that the real cap is now the Stage A support object rather than the Stage B weighting law.
